Europe in 1100: the First Crusade had just ended, and the map shows the continent's edge touching a world about to change. Here is how it started.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ In 1071 Seljuk forces beat the Byzantine army at Manzikert and captured Emperor Romanos IV. On this map the Byzantine Empire still holds the Balkans, while the Sultanate of Rum covers much of Anatolia.
2/ In March 1095 envoys of Byzantine emperor Alexios I asked for military help at the Council of Piacenza. That request led up to what happened next.
3/ On 27 November 1095 Pope Urban II gave his speech at the Council of Clermont, calling for a crusade to Jerusalem.
4/ The People's Crusade, led by Peter the Hermit, was a largely poor and untrained force. Turkish troops destroyed it at the Battle of Civetot in October 1096.
5/ The main armies beat Kilij Arslan at Dorylaeum in July 1097. They besieged Antioch from 20 October 1097 and took it in June 1098.

6/ Jerusalem fell on 15 July 1099 and a large fraction of its residents were massacred, though historians argue later sources may exaggerate the scale. Four crusader states followed: Jerusalem, Edessa, Antioch and Tripoli.
Godfrey of Bouillon took the title Defender of the Holy Sepulchre; his brother Baldwin became the first Latin king. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
